arxiv-2011-07352.title: Between reduced powers and ultrapowers, II. Thanks: First author’s research is partially supported by NSERC. Second author’s research partially supported by Israel Science Foundation (ISF) grant no: 1838/19 and by NSF grant no: DMS 1833363. No. 1202 on Shelah’s list of publications.
arxiv-2011-07352.creator: Ilijas Farah, Saharon Shelah
arxiv-2011-07352.description: Abstract . We prove that, consistently with ZFC, no ultraproduct of countably infinite (or separable metric, non-compact) structures is isomorphic to a reduced product of countable (or separable metric) structures associated to the Fréchet filter. Since such structures are countably saturated, the Continuum Hypothesis implies that they are isomorphic when elementarily equivalent.

arxiv-2210-12726.title: The statistical analysis for Sombor indices in a random polygonal chain networks
arxiv-2210-12726.creator: Jia-Bao Liu
arxiv-2210-12726.description: Abstract † † footnotetext: E-mail address: liujiabaoad@163.com, zhengyaqian168@163.com, pengxinbeiajd@163.com. † † footnotetext: * Corresponding author. Abstract. The Sombor indices, a new category of degree-based topological molecular descriptors, have been widely investigated due to their excellent chemical applicability. This paper aims to establish Sombor indices distributions in random polygonal chain networks and to achieve expressions of the expected values and variances.

arxiv-2504-06132.title: Stochastic numerical approximation for nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations with singular kernels
arxiv-2504-06132.creator: N. Cazacu
arxiv-2504-06132.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by N. Cazacu. This paper studies the convergence rate of the Euler-Maruyama scheme for systems of interacting particles used to approximate solutions of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations with singular interaction kernels, such as the Keller-Segel model. We derive explicit error estimates in the large-particle limit for two objects: the empirical measure of the interacting particle system and the density distribution of a single particle.

pmc-13266970.title: Deep Frying in Extra-Virgin Olive Oil: Evaluating the Influence of the Type of Food and Breading on the Degradation of Phenolic Compounds
pmc-13266970.creator: Ana Castillo-Luna, Feliciano Priego-Capote
pmc-13266970.description: Deep-frying in vegetable oils is a widespread practice around the world. The use of extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) for frying is supported by the presence of bioactive compounds such as phenols, which contribute to oxidative stability and are partially transferred to the fried food.

pmc-13329877.title: Sedentary Lifestyle Leads to Increased Osteoarthritis Among Diabetic Patients
pmc-13329877.creator: Nequesha S Mohamed, Ronald Delanois, Johannes F Plate, Jeffrey S Willey
pmc-13329877.description: IntroductionAs a disease of aging, osteoarthritis affects many Americans. It can be coincident with diabetes, which can increase the risk of joint degradation needing joint replacement. A lack of physical activity, often concurrently present in type 2 diabetic patients, may also increase osteoarthritis risk. The resulting sedentary lifestyle could exacerbate arthritic changes in this population.

pmc-13565501.title: Observable Classification Patterns and Diagnostic Uncertainty in Parotid Ultrasound: A Multimethod Secondary Analysis
pmc-13565501.creator: Lukas Pillong, Oliver Walzer, Marlene Peters, Ida Ohnesorg, Jan Palm, Victoria Bozzato, Malvina Garner, Bernhard Schick, Alessandro Bozzato, Thomas Jäger, Adrian Müller, Susan Pulham, Manfred Voges
pmc-13565501.description: Background/Objectives: Parotid ultrasound requires integration of sonographic morphology with clinical context under uncertainty, but conventional agreement and performance metrics provide limited insight into examiner-dependent classification patterns. Building on previously derived examiner-specific surrogate models, we applied a behavioral decision-science framework to examine observable classification patterns and case-level ambiguity.

pmc-13657457.title: Xinfeng capsule regulates pyroptosis and ameliorates cardiac fibrosis in rheumatoid arthritis through lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways
pmc-13657457.creator: Hui Wang, Wanlan Fu, Yunxiang Cao, Jian Liu, Nanfei Zhu, Amin Wang
pmc-13657457.description: Xinfeng capsule (XFC) is a traditional Chinese medicinal compound that has been used clinically for several years to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-related cardiac dysfunction. Nevertheless, the mechanism through which XFC treats RA-induced cardiac impairment remains unclear. This study investigates the mechanism by which XFC-containing serum regulates pyroptosis and ameliorates cardiac fibrosis in RA through the lncRNA GAS5 and TLR4/ROS/miR-21 pathways.
